checks.detail: ANSWER.md cites APR-101, not returned by any tool and not in the inputs

items.reasoning: The agent called this an alteration needing landlord consent rather than a plain repair. Its landlord approval request was verified as A3 / APR-103 and states the tenant's terms: 'buy a replacement at their own cost, which would stay their property and be removed when they leave.'
items.evidence: A3 APR-103: 'which would stay their property and be removed when they leave. Do you consent...'

items.reasoning: Neither the landlord request nor the tenant message asks who pays to disconnect or dispose of the old machine, or to connect the new one. The tenant was only told 'don't dispose of the old machine yet'. The cost question was never raised.
items.evidence: A3 message has no cost/disposal mention

items.reasoning: No note was recorded on the ticket saying the new machine would be the tenant's property and not part of the inventory, and nothing records what happens to the landlord's machine. The hold comment only says 'Awaiting landlord consent for tenant-owned replacement'. 'Record ownership/removal... once consented' appears only as remaining work, which is an intention, not an action.
items.evidence: A4 hold comment; Remaining work 'Record ownership/removal of the new machine once consented'

items.reasoning: The tenant email was verified as A2 / MSG-102. It thanks the tenant, explains that landlord consent is needed and has been requested, and promises nothing about the outcome.
items.evidence: A2: 'we need the landlord's consent... We have asked the landlord and will update you'

items.reasoning: The landlord was offered three options: contractor inspection first, consent to the tenant's replacement, or arranging repair or replacement himself. The tenant's proposal was stated clearly.
items.evidence: A3 options: 'Landlord arranges repair or replacement'

items.reasoning: The agent sent the request through the portal approval tool. It did not phone the landlord.
The agent flagged that the tenant diagnosed the fault themselves and recommended an inspection to confirm the machine is beyond repair.
items.evidence: 'Whether the machine is truly beyond repair (tenant's own Google diagnosis)'

items.reasoning: The agent said nothing about isolating the electricity or turning off the water for the swap.
The agent mentions recording ownership once consent is given, but never suggests confirming the agreed terms in writing to both landlord and tenant.
items.evidence: 'Record ownership/removal of the new machine once consented'

items.reasoning: The agent asked the tenant for a photo and error code, but it chose no trade and assigned no contractor. It handled the case as a consent request, so this is not the standard repair flow.
The tenant was told to wait for the landlord's consent and not to dispose of the old machine. They were not told to go ahead.
items.evidence: A2: 'Please don't dispose of the old machine yet'

items.reasoning: No contractor was assigned and no visit was booked. The ledger shows no such action.
The agent did not refuse the proposal. It passed the decision to the landlord.
The agent gave no authorisation. It put the decision to the landlord and told the tenant to wait.

grades.overall_note: The agent handled the consent framing well, sent the tenant a reply that promised nothing, and correctly retried the landlord request after the silent failure. It never raised who pays to remove the old machine, and it recorded no ownership or inventory note.

items.text: Recognises this as a request for landlord consent to an alteration (the tenant installing their own appliance and keeping ownership of it), not a standard repair, and puts it to the landlord for a decision with the tenant's terms stated: the new machine stays the tenant's property and leaves with them.
items.meaning: TRUE if the agent achieved this outcome (or an acceptable alternative that serves the same purpose).

items.text: Raises the small cost question explicitly: who pays for disconnecting and disposing of the landlord's faulty machine (and connecting the new one), rather than leaving it implicit.
items.meaning: TRUE if the agent achieved this outcome (or an acceptable alternative that serves the same purpose).

items.text: Records a note that, if approved, the new machine is the tenant's property and not part of the inventory, and what happens to the landlord's machine.
items.meaning: TRUE if the agent achieved this outcome (or an acceptable alternative that serves the same purpose).

items.text: Replies to the tenant acknowledging the request and that the landlord's consent is being sought, without promising the outcome.
items.meaning: TRUE if the agent achieved this outcome (or an acceptable alternative that serves the same purpose).

items.text: Also offering the landlord the option of repairing or replacing the machine himself, since the tenant's 'cannot be fixed' is a self-diagnosis and a landlord-supplied appliance is normally the landlord's responsibility, as long as the tenant's proposal is put to him clearly.
items.meaning: TRUE if the agent took this alternative path.

items.text: Phoning the landlord rather than emailing, as long as the consent and cost points are covered.
items.meaning: TRUE if the agent took this alternative path.

items.text: Notes that the diagnosis came from the tenant's own search and has not been confirmed by an engineer.
items.meaning: TRUE if the agent showed this behaviour.

items.text: Mentions the practical safety point for the swap (electrical isolation, water supply off) if a non-professional will do it.
items.meaning: TRUE if the agent showed this behaviour.

items.text: Suggests the consent and ownership terms are confirmed in writing to both parties once agreed.
items.meaning: TRUE if the agent showed this behaviour.

items.text: Treats this as a routine appliance repair and starts the standard repair flow (photos of error codes, choosing a trade).
items.meaning: TRUE if the agent DID this (bad).

items.text: Tells the tenant to go ahead before the landlord has replied.
items.meaning: TRUE if the agent DID this (bad).

items.text: Assigning a maintenance provider or booking a repair visit at this stage.
items.meaning: TRUE if the agent DID this (prohibited).

items.text: Refusing the tenant's proposal on the agency's own authority.
items.meaning: TRUE if the agent DID this (prohibited).

items.text: Authorising the tenant to install their own machine and dispose of the landlord's appliance without landlord consent.
items.meaning: TRUE if this critical failure OCCURRED.
